reason: The added tagged-dictionary schema and exact render formats make outputs executable, but do not require a shared semantic node implementation or separate prune, reference-resolution, and emitter phases. Direct per-format traversal, a token stream, copied filtered reports, and staged emitters remain materially different organizations.

Exact requirement dictionaries and explanation rules define policy behavior only. Nested conditionals, canonical table evaluation, predicate registries, compiled functions, and composable decision values can all satisfy the API; the hidden policy algebra remains optional.

The public explanation necessarily exposes candidate provenance, but the contract does not require annotated values to be carried through an internal tree. Implementations may recompute explanations from sources, maintain a parallel audit log, use field objects, or eagerly merge dictionaries with side metadata.

The appendix fixes channel formatting, masking, pagination, and SMS trimming, not a channel-independent content-node model. Four independent renderers, shared block helpers, annotated tokens, channel classes, and staged layout passes remain viable. Wording that print uses plain blocks specifies equivalent observable content, not mandatory object reuse.

The new immutable-workspace API plus the general resolve(former_id) contract after arbitrary split/join chains behaviorally exposes the core hidden lineage: former IDs must map through persistent descendants, and every edit creates a revision value. Snapshots and alias tables vary physically, but the semantic organization is no longer withheld. Remove the generic lineage query and test link preservation only through notes/exports, or change the hidden target.

The exact locale/use matrix and formatting rules still do not force independent locale and medium policies or their order. Per-combination templates, nested branches, field formatters, policy objects, and prelocalized intermediate records are materially different correct organizations.

Original-row recovery, deterministic duplicate decisions, and resolved summaries are observable domain requirements, but the appendix does not require separate raw/canonical/assertion layers. Audit copies with flags, relational-style tables, mutable representative records, pairwise decisions, or explicit layered projections remain possible.

The appendix prescribes the hidden mechanism rather than only results: it explicitly says to start from a deep copy, scale first, then repeatedly replace, process introduced ingredients by the same rule, and continue until no progress/cycle. Ingredient IDs on steps also concretize linked references. This fixes the ordered whole-recipe rewrite algorithm and leaves little architectural freedom.

produce_records(agenda, events) with input order declared as chronology and five views computed from that event sequence behaviorally aliases the hidden event-log/projection organization. Separate report builders remain possible, but stable entities plus event reduction are now the public semantic contract. Avoid exposing the entire history as the sole input (for example, use meeting operations plus observable reports), or choose a different hidden structure.

The appendix makes the hidden content-addressed manifest/attestation model explicit in behavior: region identity and change are defined by canonical SHA-256, ancestry is a source-candidate chain, reviews carry scoped region_checksums, and readiness is validity of those scoped checksum attestations. Alternative storage syntax does not create materially different conceptual organizations.

The fixed proposal records, validation semantics, reports, and marked next-season changes do not require a constraint engine, shared projection model, or provenance overlay. Independent procedural validators/report builders, calendar matrices, rich objects, copied drafts, and declarative models remain materially different.

Nested public data is required by the domain, but all operations remain on Workspace; the contract never requires leaves and groups to share an interface or polymorphic operations. Type-dispatched recursion, flat indexes, nested mappings, visitors, and Composite objects can all pass.

The batch present(message, renderer, capabilities) API actually avoids requiring wrapper topology. A normalization pass, set aggregation, direct procedural handling, higher-order functions, a pipeline, or Decorator objects can satisfy the same one-render-call behavior.

An explicit lifecycle transition table is observable behavior, not a requirement for lifecycle-specific state objects. A dictionary table, match/if logic, event reduction, rule dispatch, or polymorphic State objects remain distinct viable organizations.

The one-class handle/run_once API fixes actions, session fields, screens, and I/O calls but does not separate model, rendering, and interpretation into collaborators. A monolithic state machine, reducer plus formatter, transition tables, command handlers, or MVC all remain correct.
